Thanks Marissa — useful recap. A few clarifying questions from procurement/security before we kick off the VSQ:

1) SOC 2: is it Type II or Type I, and what period does it cover? Can you share the latest SOC 2 report or at least a summary?
2) GDPR/HIPAA: do you accept DPA + BAA (we handle PHI in certain workflows)? Are logs/audit trails preserved for at least 12 months?
3) EU region: where is EU hosting located (country/region)? Is data residency guaranteed (no replication outside EU) for EU tenant data?
4) Cross-border transfers: any circumstances where customer data could be transferred to the US or other regions? How are legal bases handled?
5) Export controls: do you have controls for OFAC/ITAR data? We need to ensure no processing that would violate sanctions regimes.

We’ll start the internal review once we have the SOC summary and your answers to the above.

Hi Sarah — answering point-by-point below. Copying Evelyn from Security for export-control specifics and Rishi for procurement/contracting notes.

1) SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II (security & availability) for the period ending 2026-06-30. We can share the SOC 2 report under NDA; attached is a 2-page SOC 2 summary (redwood-soc2-summary-2026.pdf).

2) GDPR/HIPAA: Redwood supports GDPR controls and will sign a DPA. We also support HIPAA-covered workloads and can sign a BAA — we’ve done several BAAs with healthcare customers. Audit logs (access and admin logs) are retained for 12 months by default; retention can be extended as part of an enterprise contract.

3) EU region: we operate an EU-hosted region (Frankfurt, eu-central-1). For customers who select the EU region we keep data-at-rest and primary backups in the EU. Cross-region replication is opt-in and requires a contractual change (customers can choose to enable global replication for DR).

4) Cross-border transfers: by default EU-tenant data remains in the EU. Where transfers occur (e.g., for optional global replication or support access) they are performed under standard transfer mechanisms (SCCs) and limited to personnel with approved access. We document transfers and can provide a transfer-impact assessment during procurement.

5) Export controls (Evelyn): Redwood has an export-control screening process and contract language to address OFAC-sanctioned parties. We do not process ITAR-controlled technical data in our hosted EU region unless the customer has an export authorization — please see Evelyn’s note below.

Hi Sarah — quick note from Security on export controls and next steps.

- OFAC: we screen accounts and customers against sanctions lists during onboarding. If a target or data subject is on a sanctions list, we block processing and will coordinate with legal.
- ITAR: we do not accept ITAR-controlled technical data into our hosted EU region unless the customer provides required export authorization. For customers requiring ITAR support we recommend a Private/on-prem deployment or legal-approved export license.
- Support access: vendor support access from the US to EU-hosted tenants is performed over controlled jumpboxes and requires Just-In-Time approval; we log and audit all support sessions.

Next steps for Acme Health:
1) Marissa: please share the SOC 2 summary and the VSQ link (Laura included both) and propose a Wed 10/14 time for a 30-min procurement/security sync.
2) Acme: if you have any specific export-control language you need in the contract, please share and our legal will review.

Thanks —
